title: Heartless
paragraphs: “Ren-san, could it be that you’re still simulating your past gaming experiences in your head?”
“N-no! I…!”
“Judging by that reaction, you must have some idea. I sometimes do the same.”

“I also remember the games I used to play. So you’re saying that in your head, you were thinking, ‘With my current strength, I could clear that quest now,’ and mentally defeating that dragon over and over?”
“And each time, the girl would be left orphaned and miserable.”
“S-shut up!”
Ren grabbed both Father and Itsuki by the shoulders, trying to stop them. I’m not one to talk, but Itsuki really doesn’t know when to stop.
“That was the past me! It has nothing to do with who I am now!”
“Why are you panicking? Calm down.”
“If he finds out that his actions led to a future where a dragon’s family—especially a young girl—was left suffering, well…”
“That’s something we absolutely have to prevent, isn’t it?”
Father and Itsuki nod as if they already understood. Ren, in particular, seems very eager.
“By the way, when Father explained how he came to take in the Assistant last time, Ren’s response was, ‘I should have killed both the parent and child.’”
“…Huh?”
Father and Itsuki turned to look at Ren in stunned silence. Ren, on the other hand, had a face that seemed to scream, “What the hell are you talking about?”
“N-no! I’m not some heartless monster!”
“Uh… We all know Motoyasu-kun doesn’t mean harm, but if we list out the events logically…”

“He killed the dragon, left the corpse to rot, causing a plague to spread, and at the same time, made the dragon’s adopted daughter suffer. Then, he even said, ‘I should have killed both the parent and child.’ That’s so heartless there’s no room for justification.”
“That’s not true!”
“Hold on, hold on. Kitamura-dono is just terrible at explaining things. I think we need to break it down more clearly to understand the full picture.”
Éclair stepped in to mediate. Father and Itsuki weren’t actually trying to condemn Ren, so they listened obediently.
“That’s true… Motoyasu-kun, could you explain in more detail? What exactly happened? What’s the story behind the dragon and this Assistant?”
“Understood. First, let me start with—”

I began explaining how, in the previous loop, Father took in the Assistant, and how the village had turned the dragon’s corpse into a tourist attraction, leading to the rotting corpse and the spread of disease. I also explained the connection between the Assistant and my rival, who had been traveling together.
“Hearing all this, it feels almost like fate.”
“Even though she was his adopted daughter, he must have cherished her deeply.”
“And? Why would I say something as horrible as ‘I should have killed both parent and child’? If this keeps up, I won’t even understand myself anymore…”
“That was after we took down the Three Heroes Church and during the Level-Up Event on Cal Mira Island.”
“We swapped party members to foster friendship between the heroes.”
“That’s when the Assistant and Ren ended up clashing.”
“Ah… so he relied on his game knowledge and went solo?”
“If Ren fought the same way he used to, that would be terrifying for teamwork. It’s less about synchronizing with others and more about forcing others to keep up with him…”
“Well, Ren has improved now. He can see his surroundings better and work in sync with everyone.”
“Hmph… So what happened next?”

“During a battle with monsters, the Assistant found him a nuisance and shoved him aside. Ren got furious and yelled, but the Assistant had already reached their limit and ended up beating him to a pulp.”
That clash undeniably created a decisive rift.

However… even without that friction, Ren and Itsuki likely would have broken the seals of the Four Guardian Beasts. If they acted based on their game knowledge, it would have seemed like the right move. It was around the time when they would naturally feel compelled to take on such a challenge.
“So, you only learned about this later? Ren has strong self-preservation instincts, so if he sees someone as an enemy, he might blurt something out without thinking…”
“I see, that makes sense.”
“You should’ve told me before we swapped party members! Even I would’ve at least hesitated! …I would’ve, right?”
“The timing was just bad. The Assistant didn’t want anything to do with you either.”
Everything was just bad timing. Even Father’s attempts to smooth things over were meaningless.
Still… if it had only ended with their defeat against the Phoenix or Spirit Tortoise, the mistake could have been managed. No one could have predicted that the seals would break one after another.
“Anyway, now that I know all this, I’ll never make the same mistake.”
“Yeah. Besides, we already have plenty of dragon-related materials, so there’s no need to go out of our way to hunt that dragon.”
“That’s true, but… hasn’t everything been locked ever since we got Fitoria’s feather?”
“All the Filolial-type weapons seem to have been unlocked, though.”
“That huge Filolial really left us with some troublesome parting gifts.”
Ren grumbled. He seemed a little irritated.
“Still… Ren-san.”
“What, Itsuki? Don’t look at me with those gentle eyes.”
“I don’t think I’ve ever felt a stronger sense of camaraderie with you than I do today.”
“Should I really be happy about that…?”
“Indeed. Iwatani-dono’s point is quite reasonable.”

“By the way, when we returned from the island, Éclair’s funeral was taking place. She was imprisoned and ended up dying in her cell, a victim of the Three Heroes Church’s spite after Father’s achievements angered them.”
“Ugh… Amaki-dono, Kawasumi-dono, it seems I, too, am now one of your comrades.”
Éclair approached Ren and Itsuki, joining hands with them. A sense of solidarity had formed.
“Man, this is something else…”
Father watched the scene with distant eyes. For a while afterward, a self-deprecating conversation unfolded, including how he was first deceived by that crimson swine.
“Getting back to the topic, unlocking the lock would be easier if you make the rival an ally.”
“Is that so?”
“I don’t use dragon-type material weapons myself, but I’ve heard they’re necessary for unlocking it.”
Ren pondered over my words.
Was there some inconsistency in what I had said?
“But… can it be persuaded? It was supposed to be a relatively weak dragon…”
“It called itself the ‘Weakest Dragon Emperor’.”
“Is that something to brag about?”
“Anyway, it’s best to follow the instructions first, isn’t it?”
“That was my plan from the start. I’ll try approaching it like taming it.”
“A huge dragon as an ally? …That would make travel much easier.”
“But it’s the weakest one, right? If it suddenly got shot down and crashed to its death, that wouldn’t even be funny.”
“We just need to strengthen its base abilities, like we did with Yuki and the others.”
Since we traveled via portal, we didn’t have a carriage with us. Everyone was riding Filolials for transport.
Should we find a carriage somewhere?
“I hate dragons!”
“Indeed, they are quite smelly.”
“Kou hates them too!”
“Still, this is a necessary step, so try to endure it… okay?”
It reminded me of Sakura from the last time. She suffered hair and feather loss due to stress. Thanks to Father’s efforts, she had recovered to some extent.
“Aren’t they reacting like they’re being bullied?”
“It seems their mutual dislike is real.”
“Indeed. Filolials and dragons simply cannot understand each other on a genetic level.”
“Then what do we do?! Why do you always say such careless things, Motoyasu-san?”
“Calm down, Itsuki. He’s always dumped everything on Naofumi anyway. No point in complaining now.”
“Oh, you’ve finally caught on. As for your question, Itsuki, I think we should just use the spear to threaten it into joining us.”
I said that, and they all sighed. For some reason, the conversation ended there. Meanwhile, Father seemed to be talking with Sakura and the others.
“Ugh…”
“Well, if we get too close to the dragon’s habitat, we can have Sakura and the others wait somewhere safe.”
“No! I can’t just sit around if Naofumi might get hurt by a dragon!”
“I refuse.”
“Kou won’t wait either!”
Father looked troubled by their response. He was kind, after all. He probably couldn’t bring himself to scold them unfairly.
“Motoyasu-san, could you… ah, never mind, you definitely wouldn’t scold them.”
“They worship him, after all.”
“This is a hassle. Can’t Naofumi do something about it?”
“Hmm, if this keeps up, we’ll be going in circles.”
“A-Anyway, everyone, can you try to endure it for just a little while?”
“…Fine.”

Filolials were intelligent beings. They wouldn’t throw tantrums over something like this. Still, Itsuki stopped short of saying something to me… but he wasn’t wrong. I could ask the Filolials for favors, but scolding them was impossible for me.
“While we’re at it, Naofumi-san, could you ask Kou to stop messing with my hair?”
“You can do that yourself.”
“I tried, but she won’t listen.”
“Hmm… I’ll ask later, but no promises.”
“The previous Father managed to discipline Kou, I say.”
“There you have it, Motoyasu-san said so. Please do something about it.”
“Sigh… fine. But aren’t you two using me a little too conveniently?”
That night, Father did ask Kou to stop, but… she didn’t really listen.
